s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with exertion, associated with evidence of myocardial ischemia
salient_findings: Substernal chest pain triggered by running more than 2 miles
ST depressions during recovery phase of exercise treadmill test
Severe ischemia in the distribution of the left anterior descending and circumflex arteries on PET-MPI
key_facts: Hypertension controlled with lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide
No family history of premature coronary artery disease
High exercise capacity during treadmill test

shortlist.label: Three-vessel obstructive coronary artery disease
shortlist.why_kept: CCTA showed 3-vessel involvement and coronary angiogram confirmed findings, matching the patient's symptoms and test results

shortlist.label: Chronic stable angina
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms of chest pain with exertion and evidence of myocardial ischemia on PET-MPI are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Unstable angina
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms and test results, including ST depressions during recovery phase of ETT, could also suggest unstable angina

shortlist.label: Acute coronary syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms and evidence of myocardial ischemia could be indicative of an acute coronary syndrome, although the clinical context suggests a more chronic condition

shortlist.label: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely, this rare condition could still be considered given the patient's symptoms and evidence of coronary artery disease

raw.rationale: The patient's CCTA showed 3-vessel involvement and the coronary angiogram confirmed these findings, indicating significant coronary artery disease. The patient's symptoms and test results, including ST depressions during the recovery phase of the exercise treadmill test and severe ischemia shown on PET-MPI, are consistent with this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Chronic stable angina
rejected.why: While the patient has angina, the presence of 3-vessel involvement and severe ischemia suggests a more complex condition than stable angina alone.

rejected.label: Unstable angina
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms do not indicate unstable angina, as the chest pain is not increasing in frequency or severity and occurs only with significant exertion.

rejected.label: Acute coronary syndrome
rejected.why: There is no indication of an acute myocardial infarction or other signs of an acute coronary syndrome in the provided information.

rejected.label: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection
rejected.why: There is no evidence to suggest a dissection, and the patient's presentation and test results are more consistent with atherosclerotic disease.
